claims.text: The additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has a dual-nanoprecipitation microstructure.
The alloy has a fine, heterogeneous matrix containing coherent nanoprecipitates.
APT can elucidate the mechanistic role of nanoprecipitates during high-temperature oxidation of Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3.
APT can resolve compositional gradients and elemental redistribution at nanoprecipitate–matrix interfaces.
Isothermal oxidation at 850–1050 °C in laboratory air is an applicable test condition for studying this alloy.
Oxidized specimens can be prepared as needles for APT analysis.
Nanoprecipitates may preferentially enrich or deplete Cr, Al, or Ti at their interfaces.
Interfacial elemental partitioning at nanoprecipitates mediates the nucleation and growth of protective or nonprotective oxides.
Oxidation produces localized diffusion gradients and elemental redistribution around nanoprecipitates.
APT provides near-atomic-resolution compositional measurements of oxidation-induced gradients.
Cr or Al enrichment near nanoprecipitates promotes protective oxide-scale formation, whereas regions lacking such segregation form less protective oxides.
APT will detect distinct elemental-segregation patterns at nanoprecipitate interfaces in oxidized Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3.
Interfacial Cr or Al enrichment will correlate with enhanced protective-oxide formation and reduced oxidation rates relative to cast or wrought material.
Conventionally cast or wrought variants have coarser microstructures because of slower cooling kinetics.
Cast or wrought variants exhibit less pronounced nanoscale elemental partitioning than additively manufactured material.
APT analysis of mixed oxide/metal interfaces is limited by specimen-preparation challenges and differential field-evaporation behavior.
Measured segregation patterns may vary with oxidation temperature and time.
APT artifacts and limited dynamic range for oxygen-rich phases may impede quantitative linkage between segregation and oxidation kinetics.
TEM-EDS may be required to validate APT measurements of oxide-scale chemistry.
